best.plan_strategy: Attempt 1: replace the linear baseline with a gradient-boosted tree ensemble (hist_gbdt) fitted on the full training split, with class_weight='balanced' to move the default cut toward recall. The goal bar (0.9194 balanced_accuracy) sits above the baseline's ranking ceiling (0.8266), so the whole point of this attempt is to generate a better ranking: a GBDT on adult reliably reaches roc_auc ~0.927-0.93 versus logreg's 0.908, and it can capture the non-linear/interaction structure (education-num x hours-per-week x marital-status/relationship, the spike-at-zero capital-gain/loss) that a scaled linear model on one-hot columns cannot express. Configuration: max_iter=400, learning_rate=0.06, max_leaf_nodes=31, l2_regularization=1.0, early_stopping=false so all 29,304 training rows are used and this attempt's score is comparable with later ones; impute='none' so hist_gbdt splits on NaN in workclass/occupation/native-country itself (no missing_indicator alongside it — the card states that is bit-for-bit redundant), and scale=false since trees are scale-invariant. Read the reported roc_auc / pr_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against the baseline's 0.908 / 0.7723 / 0.8266 to size how much of the required ranking lift (KS 0.6531 -> 0.8388) one family swap actually buys, and read cut_headroom together with recall vs specificity to see whether any of the residual gap is on the operating-point axis before touching the weighting again in attempt 2.

critic.evidence: Attempt 1 (hist_gbdt, class_weight='balanced') scored balanced_accuracy 0.8442 (95% CI 0.8362~0.8517) against the bar 0.9194 — a shortfall of 0.0752, far outside the CI width 0.0155. The family swap did lift the ranking as planned: roc_auc 0.9272 vs the baseline's 0.908, pr_auc 0.8288 vs 0.7723, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8451 vs the baseline ceiling 0.8266 (KS 0.6531 -> ~0.6902), but the bar demands KS 0.8388, so ~0.149 of ranking lift is still missing. The operating point is exhausted: cut_headroom is 0.000936, i.e. 1.2% of the remaining 0.0752, and recall 0.8567 vs specificity 0.8317 are already nearly equal, so no class_weight or threshold move can buy more than ~0.001. train_val_gap is only 0.0444 (train_balanced_accuracy 0.8886 vs val 0.8442), so this is not overfitting and not a capacity/regularisation problem; train itself (0.8886) sits below the bar, so more of the same family's hyperparameter space cannot reach 0.9194 either. Sizing the remaining lever: the ranking ceiling has been observed across families at 0.8266 (logreg) to 0.8451 (hist_gbdt), a span of 0.0185, while the distance still to go is 0.0752 — roughly 4x that span, and prior family swaps moved roc_auc only 0.0022–0.0077 against a paired resolution of 0.003–0.006. No hyperparameters were dropped (dropped_hyperparams empty), runtime 13.7 s is nowhere near the budget, and calibration_error 0.0986 / brier 0.1081 indicate overconfidence that the registry cannot correct here.
critic.direction: The gap is entirely on the ranking axis, so stop touching the operating point and spend the next attempt on a different strong tabular family — fit xgboost under the same NaN-native pipeline (impute='none', scale=false, no indicator columns) with scale_pos_weight left at the class ratio, to measure whether a second family's ranking ceiling moves at all; be aware the bar is ~9x larger than any family swap measured so far, so the realistic outcome is a small ranking gain rather than reaching 0.9194.

critic.evidence: Iteration 2 (xgboost, depth 7, 900 rounds, lr 0.04, scale_pos_weight 3.18) scored balanced_accuracy 0.8418 (95% CI 0.8342~0.8501, width 0.0158) against the bar 0.9194 — a shortfall of 0.0776, five times the CI width. The paired Δ vs iteration 1 is -0.0024 (95% CI -0.0068~+0.0020, P(better) 0.145), so the family swap produced movement this slice cannot resolve from zero: roc_auc 0.9255 vs 0.9272, pr_auc 0.8265 vs 0.8288, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8436 vs 0.8451 — all inside the resolution. The operating point is again spent: cut_headroom 0.001841 is 2% of the remaining 0.0776, and recall 0.8383 vs specificity 0.8453 are nearly equal, so no class_weight/scale_pos_weight move buys more than ~0.002. Nothing was dropped (dropped_hyperparams empty), runtime 10.7 s of 600 s, so neither cost nor a silently unapplied key explains anything. What is different from the last verdict: I prescribed wrong_model_family once and it paid nothing — the two families' balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut now span only 0.8436~0.8451 (0.0015) while the distance from the best cut to the bar is 0.0743, i.e. 50x that span, and KS stands at 0.6902 against the required 0.8388. So a third family off the same list is arithmetically not a route to 0.9194 and I am not prescribing one. The only untried lever the executor actually has is information in the columns (missing_count / missing_indicator with imputation), and on this file that is worth roughly a hundredth at best; the depth-7 run also raised train_val_gap to 0.0783 (train 0.9200 vs val 0.8418) while the val score fell, so added capacity is now being absorbed as memorisation rather than ranking.
critic.direction: Stop buying family swaps — the two measured ranking ceilings differ by 0.0015 against a 0.0743 remaining distance — and spend one attempt on the only untried information lever, adding missing_count as a single extra column while holding the family and hyperparameters exactly at iteration 1's hist_gbdt configuration so the row is attributable to that preprocessing change alone; if it does not move outside the 0.0158 width, the 0.9194 bar is above what these 14 columns support and the remaining iterations should consolidate on iteration 1's settings.
